item.title: Re: +1
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for the upvote and the nice comment!

Incidentally, this tale was originally going to be a mainsite article or potentially a joke article, but the consensus from reviewers was that the story of the investigation was more entertaining than the material in the SCP documentation itself.
I don't think I've seen the writing process of an SCP article being done from an in-universe point of view before. I reaöly enjoyed this.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Nitpicks:

Riven outright laughed.

Overplaying. Just have him snicker.

Surprising that it knew about legendary swords, though.

Not really sure why this is surprising, though I could potentially believe it. Just seems odd to single out. I mean, we know famous human historical figures, right? Maybe add a line or something.

And none of the other interviews seem to give as much information about the object.

Exposition not necessary.

“Do you think it’ll ever speak again?”

Odd question. It's only been seven days, why wouldn't it speak again?

We don’t even know if it’s the sword itself that was talking, or something inhabiting the sword that just up and left.”

Covered that already in the story (but this one's better, could probably cut the earlier instance, but not the biggest deal).

I really like the closing lines, but they could stand to have at least one or dialogue tags to keep us grounded.

Saying "item has ceased to exhibit effects" without at least waiting a little bit longer seems really premature.

Beyond that, I love this piece. Quite entertaining and funny.

item.title: Author Notes
item.content:encoded:
Many thanks to Tuomey, Dmatix, Eskobar, Photosynthetic, The Raven, Vince, ProcyonLotor, DrYucatan, Randomini, and anyone else who read it over in chat whom I may have forgotten and if so I am sorry. Title was picked by Aelanna, who convinced me with “It has a double meaning, because a Check is also a movement in fencing.”

This started off as an SCP article, but that format didn’t quite suit the story I wanted to tell, which was basically “Foundation studies thing, Foundation effectively breaks thing, Foundation pretty much keeps studying thing.” Also, I wanted to touch upon the in-universe process of writing up an SCP article, and the inherent possibility that the Foundation has a lot of other broken things in storage (including living things).

Also, swords. I did a lot of reading research about swords. For the record, it’d be called a bastard sword, or so I’m told.
